questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while driving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: How should you keep a parked trailer from moving if it does not have spring brakes?
questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks to stop a parked trailer without spring brakes from moving. Air brakes only work as long as there is air pressure. Wheel chocks provide the safest way to keep the trailer in place.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: a service line and an emergency line.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need extra space on the road?

options.text: They drive slower than other commercial vehicles.
They are heavier than other commercial vehicles.
They need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles. Managing space properly is very important when driving these vehicles.

questions.question: What can the crack-the-whip effect do?
questions.explanation: The crack-the-whip effect can cause a trailer to tip over during a lane change. To avoid this, drivers should change lanes slowly and safely.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?

options.text: It is a square blue knob.
It is a triangular yellow knob.
It is an eight-sided red knob.
It is a circular orange knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is an eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control on newer vehicles is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: When do large combination vehicles take the longest time to stop?
questions.explanation: Large combination vehicles take longer to stop when empty than when loaded. Empty vehicles have less weight, which reduces tire traction on the road.

questions.question: During a trip, which valve should be open?
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, keep all shut-off valves open except the last ones on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all trailer brakes and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: What can the crack-the-whip effect do?
questions.explanation: The crack-the-whip effect can cause trailers to tip over. The last trailer in a combination is most likely to tip over from this effect. Drivers should know how their vehicle responds to this and drive carefully.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space

questions.explanation: Before each trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: Often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Protects the tractor from being stolen
Protects the tractor from exceeding a set speed
Keeps air in the braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak
Ensures oil adequately lubricates the engine

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.
To test the lights on the trailer.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. When pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency trailer brakes activate automatically.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color identifies emergency or supply lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help drivers couple correctly. Blue is typically used for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: When backing your tractor under a trailer during coupling, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Safe coupling and uncoupling is very important. Before backing your tractor under the trailer, make sure the trailer brakes are locked.

questions.question: If the trailer's spring brakes do not release when you press the tractor air supply control, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.explanation: All vehicle equipment must work properly before you drive. If the trailer's spring brakes do not release when you push in the tractor air supply control, check that the air line connections are attached and sealed properly.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.explanation: If the trailer begins to jackknife, release the brakes and let the trailer wheels regain traction. Do not use the trailer hand brake because it will only make the skid worse. Applying brakes is what locked the wheels in the first place.
